exceptions.reason: Shared test infrastructure isolates Git and process state, seeds acceptance and migrated-store fixtures, coordinates SQLite neighbors, derives schema budgets, and names corpus coverage. Production dependencies' tests import these helpers directly or through another declared helper; the checker derives those uses and refuses an orphaned declaration. None belongs in the shipped command dependency set.

CD-0008 permits read-only point-in-time reconstruction for audit and diagnosis, CD-0013 D13 defines the mechanism, and .concord/docs/floor-readiness.v1.json cites it as fc5 evidence. The WF36 corpus scenario proves it folds a subject's event prefix without mutating live state. R4 row 12 classifies an operator surface for point-in-time diagnosis as a post-spine tool candidate, so no verb is owed before the floor. ReconstructSubjectAt is the entry point; its private helpers include productsForProject, which populates reconstructed Project membership, and upcastEvent.

Both are assertion helpers for registry conformance tests. knownSubjectTypes enumerates the subject kinds an event may carry, and validateEventKindRegistry rejects an ill-formed event-kind registration. Neither guards a production path: they run where a malformed registration can actually be written, which is in a test that constructs one deliberately. Exposing either to an operator would offer a verb whose only honest answer is that the build already settled the question.

Production never injects a definition registry: cmd/concord enters through Invoke, which dispatches on the builtin registry. This seam lets the workflow corpus boundary runner drive a scenario registry through the real byte-oriented boundary instead of reaching past it. The tested seam remains until its disposition is decided.

BuiltinWorkflowDefinitions supplies the live authoring heads to scripts/workflow-action-contracts; BuiltinWorkflowDefinitionsWithHistory supplies frozen schema references. CI runs generate-agent-contracts.py --check to verify both projections. The analysis roots ./cmd/... only and cannot see these build-time edges. Runtime capture resolves live families through LiveWorkflowDefinitionForRef and the full registry; builtinWorkflowDefinitionsWithHistory stays runtime-reachable through NewBuiltinWorkflowRegistry.

These pure accessors supply canonical recovery payloads, cross-field declarations, and guard-owned teaching to scripts/workflow-action-contracts. The projector generates the authoring contract from the engine-owned fields and rules; it grants no runtime admission. The analysis roots ./cmd/... only and cannot see this build-time edge. CI runs generate-agent-contracts.py --check to detect projection drift. Core preflight and recovery validation retain the runtime field and cross-field owners.

Agent tests (overlap_guard_scope_test.go, observation_law_revision_boundary_test.go) assert the Domain-overlap admission refusal outside a mutation, and the check that produces it, checkWorkflowDomainOverlapTxAdmitting, is unexported. The exported production read QueryDomainOverlaps returns overlap pairs, not that refusal. The seam runs the same check under readSnapshot with a queryer-only callback, so inspection takes no write lock and restates no rule.

Current-placement entry points the knowledge-manifest bindings call. The path prefix became a parameter (CD-0194 D5) so history composes under the tier its revision carries, and these zero-argument forms pin the tier authored law uses: TestKnowledgeManifestIneligiblePathsMatchSchema and the vocabulary tests bind them to contracts/concord-knowledge-index.v1.schema.json, so the schema keeps one validated restatement per tier instead of each test restating the prefix.

CD-0216 Consequences names this direct-caller form: direct callers use the sole pack-operation idempotency boundary (beginResearchMutation and finishResearchMutation over idempotency_records), and agent envelopes compose its transaction-scoped cores with envelope-owned idempotency. Production reaches only those WithinTx cores through internal/agent research mutations; research_test.go and the agent research fixtures call these forms. Deleting them needs an amendment to that CD-0216 sentence.

CD-0200 governs mandated-law home and conflict checks. Runtime admission uses the transaction-scoped boundary; the law-boundary tests exercise these pooled-connection entry points, including knowledge source-set freshness. These test seams and their private helpers preserve that boundary's independent assertions without opening a second runtime admission path.

DatabaseForTesting is the declared raw-handle seam for tests and pm1fixture; boundary_test.go enforces that production callers do not use it. DurableCommits is the test introspection read for the durable commit mechanism CD-0207 governs, exercised by durable_test.go. Neither is an operator mutation surface, and deleting them would remove the surviving assertions rather than retire a runtime feature.
